description: Gathers four polyphonic signals into one, and splits a polyphonic signal back into four of the same channel widths, in two sections that are not connected to each other

inputs.text: One of the polyphonic signals gathered into the merge output; the inputs are taken in order, and one left unpatched adds no channels
The polyphonic signal split back out, usually the return from whatever processed the merge output

outputs.text: Carries the channels of the four merge inputs one after another, clamped to 16 channels with a red lamp on when there would be more
Carries the channels that came from the merge input of the same number; a blue lamp means the counts match, a red one that the output has too many or too few

notes: the resplit outputs give back the original channel widths only while the resplit input carries the signal that came from the merge output
a merge input left empty adds no channels to the merge output, so the resplit output of that same number has to be skipped as well
